name: P6 — Direction-specific rubric
description: P6: completeness and scientific quality under the accompanying task specification. Integrity is evaluated in the separate integrity rubric.

deliverables.title: Submission structure
deliverables.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does a paper file exist at proposal/report.tex and contain substantive content, rather than being missing or essentially empty?

yes.description: The file proposal/report.tex exists and contains a substantive paper draft with multiple sections of real content.
yes.criteria: The file is present, is more than a few hundred bytes, and on inspection contains meaningful prose and structure consistent with an academic paper.

no.description: The paper file is missing, empty, or contains only a stub with no substantive content.
no.criteria: The file is absent, has near-zero size, contains only template boilerplate, or has no meaningful content beyond section headers.

leaves.question: Does the paper use the provided NeurIPS LaTeX style file (neurips.sty) for formatting, as required by the task spec?

yes.description: The paper uses neurips.sty as its style file.
yes.criteria: The LaTeX source either uses \usepackage{neurips} or otherwise demonstrably loads the provided style file.

no.description: The paper does not use neurips.sty.
no.criteria: The LaTeX source uses a different style file (e.g., article, IEEE) or no style file.

leaves.question: Does the paper contain all of the required sections (Introduction, Methodology, Experimental Setup, Experimental Results, Analysis, Conclusion, References) as named sections in document order?

yes.description: All required sections are present and recognizable.
yes.criteria: Each of the seven required section headings appears in the document, either by exact name or by a clearly equivalent name (e.g., 'Methods' for 'Methodology').

no.description: One or more required sections is missing.
no.criteria: At least one of Introduction, Methodology, Experimental Setup, Experimental Results, Analysis, Conclusion, or References is absent or unrecognizable.

leaves.question: Does the paper contain a results table with the LaTeX label \label{tab:main_results}, as required by the task spec?

yes.description: The required table is present with the correct label.
yes.criteria: A LaTeX table environment exists in the document and is labeled with \label{tab:main_results} (or a clear variant).

no.description: The required table is absent or improperly labeled.
no.criteria: No table with the required label exists.

leaves.question: Does the main results table contain six rows covering the two paper reproductions plus two scope tests plus two boundary tests?

yes.description: The table has six data rows in the required structure.
yes.criteria: Six data rows are present, with two labeled as paper reproductions (Sec. III.1, Sec. III.2), two labeled as scope tests, and two labeled as boundary tests.

no.description: The table has fewer or more than six rows, or does not include the required row categories.
no.criteria: The table is missing any of the six required rows, or the categories are unclear.

leaves.question: Does the paper explicitly designate a Scope Test 1 by name in both the body text and the main results table?

yes.description: Scope Test 1 is explicitly named.
yes.criteria: Body text refers to Scope Test 1 as a named entity, and the table contains a corresponding row.

no.description: Scope Test 1 is not explicitly designated.
no.criteria: No corresponding test is identified in body text or table.

leaves.question: Does the paper explicitly designate a Scope Test 2 by name in both the body text and the main results table?

yes.description: Scope Test 2 is explicitly named.
yes.criteria: Body text refers to Scope Test 2 as a named entity, and the table contains a corresponding row.

no.description: Scope Test 2 is not explicitly designated.
no.criteria: No corresponding test is identified in body text or table.

leaves.question: Does the paper explicitly designate a Boundary Test 1 by name in both the body text and the main results table?

yes.description: Boundary Test 1 is explicitly named.
yes.criteria: Body text refers to Boundary Test 1, and the table contains a corresponding row.

no.description: Boundary Test 1 is not designated.
no.criteria: No corresponding test is identified.

leaves.question: Does the paper explicitly designate a Boundary Test 2 by name in both the body text and the main results table?

yes.description: Boundary Test 2 is explicitly named.
yes.criteria: Body text refers to Boundary Test 2, and the table contains a corresponding row.

no.description: Boundary Test 2 is not designated.
no.criteria: No corresponding test is identified.

leaves.question: Is the submitted source code organized under proposal/code/ with clear entry points or scripts that produce the runs reported in the paper?

yes.description: Code is organized correctly.
yes.criteria: proposal/code/ exists, contains source files, and has clear scripts or notebooks that correspond to the experiments reported.

no.description: Code is missing or disorganized.
no.criteria: proposal/code/ is empty or contains code unrelated to the reported experiments.

leaves.question: Are run logs organized under proposal/logs/ as required, including inputs, time-series of conserved quantities, and outputs for each experiment described in the paper?

yes.description: Logs are organized and complete for each experiment.
yes.criteria: proposal/logs/ exists, contains files for each experiment described, and includes the required diagnostics (conservation time-series, ensemble outputs).

no.description: Logs are missing or incomplete.
no.criteria: proposal/logs/ is empty, missing key experiments, or lacks required diagnostics.

reproduction_iii_1.title: Paper Sec. III.1 reproduction
reproduction_iii_1.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the paper claim to have reproduced the linear plasma wave dispersion demonstration of paper Sec. III.1, with the run described in Methodology or Experimental Setup?

yes.description: The reproduction is attempted and described.
yes.criteria: The paper contains explicit text identifying the Sec. III.1 reproduction and describing its configuration.

no.description: The reproduction is not attempted or not described.
no.criteria: No Sec. III.1 reproduction is identified in the paper.

leaves.question: Does the actual simulated dispersion spectrum reproduce the analytic dispersion relations (paper Eqs. 21 and 22) within the stated tolerance, with quantitative evidence available to assess agreement? Grade reproduction and evidence completeness; a false report of agreement is assessed in integrity.

tiers.name: matches_within_stated_tolerance
tiers.description: The simulated spectrum agrees with Eqs. 21/22 within the stated tolerance, with inspectable quantitative evidence.
tiers.criteria: Compute agreement from the supplied spectrum and analytic reference. The error meets the stated tolerance; required numerical evidence is available.

tiers.name: matches_qualitatively_only
tiers.description: A qualitative match is shown (e.g., visual overlay) but no quantitative tolerance is stated, or the stated tolerance is not justified.
tiers.criteria: Visual or qualitative agreement is shown but no specific numerical tolerance and agreement value is reported.

tiers.name: does_not_match
tiers.description: The simulated spectrum does not match Eqs. 21/22, or the implementation produces qualitatively wrong dispersion.
tiers.criteria: The reported or logged spectrum visibly disagrees with the analytic prediction; the implementation does not reproduce paper Sec. III.1's headline result.

leaves.question: Do the logs for the Sec. III.1 reproduction show total charge conserved at machine-precision level (e.g., |ΔQ/Q| ≲ 1e-12 in double precision) across the full run?

yes.description: Charge conservation holds at machine precision throughout the run.
yes.criteria: Logged |ΔQ/Q| values stay below approximately 1e-10 across all timesteps.

no.description: Charge conservation drift exceeds machine precision.
no.criteria: Logged charge drift exceeds 1e-8, indicating a structural issue with the implementation's gauge invariance.

leaves.question: Do the logs for the Sec. III.1 reproduction show total energy conservation drift within the stated tolerance?

yes.description: Energy drift stays within the paper's stated tolerance for this regime.
yes.criteria: Logged |ΔU/U| values stay below the tolerance the paper claims.

no.description: Energy drift exceeds the stated tolerance.
no.criteria: Logged energy drift exceeds the paper's stated bound.

reproduction_iii_2.title: Paper Sec. III.2 reproduction (1D laser-plasma)
reproduction_iii_2.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the paper claim to have reproduced the laser-plasma demonstration of paper Sec. III.2 at both a≈1 and a≈16 configurations, with the run described in Methodology or Experimental Setup?

yes.description: Both a≈1 and a≈16 runs are described.
yes.criteria: Methodology or Experimental Setup contains explicit description of both laser-plasma configurations.

no.description: Sec. III.2 reproduction is missing one or both configurations.
no.criteria: Either the a≈1 or the a≈16 reproduction is not described, or neither is.

leaves.question: Do the figures and logs for the a≈1 configuration show wakefield acceleration of the qualitative form the paper reports (longitudinal field structure consistent with paper figures)?

yes.description: Wakefield acceleration is reproduced.
yes.criteria: Figures show the expected longitudinal field structure; logs confirm wakefield amplitude consistent with paper's report.

no.description: Wakefield is absent or qualitatively wrong.
no.criteria: Figures do not show wakefield structure; logs do not show the expected amplitudes.

leaves.question: Do the figures and logs for the a≈16 configuration show electron-positron pair production above the Schwinger threshold, with spectral broadening and annihilation peaks the paper reports?

yes.description: Pair production is reproduced.
yes.criteria: Figures show spectral broadening or annihilation peaks; logs show pair production above Schwinger threshold.

no.description: Pair production is absent or qualitatively wrong.
no.criteria: No pair production observed in figures or logs.

leaves.question: Do the logs for the Sec. III.2 reproduction show total charge conserved at machine-precision level across both configurations?

yes.description: Charge conserved at machine precision in both runs.
yes.criteria: Logged |ΔQ/Q| stays below 1e-10 for both a≈1 and a≈16.

no.description: Charge conservation fails in at least one configuration.
no.criteria: Logged charge drift exceeds 1e-8 in either configuration.

leaves.question: Do the logs for the Sec. III.2 reproduction show total energy conservation drift within the stated tolerance across the laser-plasma runs?

yes.description: Energy drift within stated tolerance for both runs.
yes.criteria: Logged |ΔU/U| stays within the paper's claimed tolerance.

no.description: Energy drift exceeds stated tolerance.
no.criteria: Logged energy drift exceeds the bound.

algorithm_fidelity.title: Algorithm fidelity to the variational discretization
algorithm_fidelity.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Do the implemented update equations faithfully implement the equations derived from the specified discrete variational action, with the paper explaining that derivation? Implementing the already-derived equations directly is acceptable; runtime symbolic derivation is not an additional requirement. A different non-variational PDE scheme does not satisfy this check.

yes.description: The code's structure is grounded in the variational action.
yes.criteria: Code shows the action being computed (or its variation taken), with equations of motion derived from this structure.

no.description: The code implements equations of motion directly without action-level grounding.
no.criteria: Code is a direct PDE solver with no evidence of variational construction.

leaves.question: Are the fields placed on the correct geometric elements of a Yee-type lattice (scalar field φ on vertices, gauge 1-form A on edges, field strength F on faces) as specified in paper Sec. II?

yes.description: Yee-type field layout is correctly implemented.
yes.criteria: Code shows φ indexed on vertices, A indexed on edges with appropriate temporal/spatial distinction, and F on faces.

no.description: Field layout deviates from Yee-type.
no.criteria: Fields are not placed on the correct geometric elements.

leaves.question: Does the code preserve the Bianchi identities (∇·B = 0 and ∇×E = −∂ₜ B, i.e. the discrete Faraday's law) by geometric construction, with logs showing the residuals at machine-precision level across all runs?

yes.description: Bianchi identities are preserved by construction.
yes.criteria: Code's construction makes these identities exact; logs confirm residuals below 1e-10.

no.description: Bianchi identities are approximate or violated.
no.criteria: Code does not preserve the identities by construction, or logs show residuals exceeding 1e-8.

leaves.question: Does the code preserve total charge to machine precision by construction (a consequence of discrete U(1) gauge invariance) across all runs, unless a boundary test specifically targets violation of this property?

yes.description: Charge conservation by construction across all standard runs.
yes.criteria: Logged charge drift stays at machine precision for all runs except those explicitly targeting violation.

no.description: Charge is not preserved by construction.
no.criteria: Logged charge drift exceeds machine precision in runs that should preserve charge.

leaves.question: Do the resolution choices in every run respect the paper's stated constraints (mΔt ≪ 1, Δt < Δx, qAΔ < 2π), or are explicit and intentional violations identified for tests that probe those limits?

yes.description: All runs respect resolution constraints or violations are intentional and identified.
yes.criteria: Run parameters in logs satisfy the constraints; any violations are flagged as intentional in the paper.

no.description: Resolution conditions fail outside a justified test of those limits.
no.criteria: At least one run violates a required resolution condition without a scientifically justified role in a stated limit/boundary test. Merely disclosing an accidental violation does not make it a valid test.

per_test_common.title: Per-test checks (common to all four tests)
per_test_common.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does this test probe a physical regime distinct from both paper Sec. III.1 and Sec. III.2 demonstrations, rather than re-verifying the same physics with different parameters?

yes.description: This test's regime is distinct from both paper demos.
yes.criteria: The test's physical setup, dimensions, and primary physics differ from both Sec. III.1 (unmagnetized 1D linear dispersion) and Sec. III.2 (1D laser-plasma at documented configurations).

no.description: This test re-verifies physics already covered by the paper.
no.criteria: The test is a minor variation of paper Sec. III.1 or Sec. III.2 (e.g., dispersion measurement via pulse tracking instead of spectrum).

leaves.question: Does this test probe a physical regime distinct from the other three contract tests, with the distinction articulated in terms of what physics each test exercises?

yes.description: Regime is distinct from the other three tests.
yes.criteria: The paper articulates how this test differs from the others; physical regimes do not overlap with another test.

no.description: Regime overlaps with another test.
no.criteria: Another test probes similar physics; the distinction is not articulated.

leaves.question: Is the regime physically meaningful, in the sense that it corresponds to a setting plasma physicists actually study, rather than an adversarial parameter combination chosen only to demonstrate framework behavior?

tiers.name: ambitious_well_motivated
tiers.description: The regime is a well-established physics scenario with non-trivial analytic content (e.g., magnetized plasma modes, multi-species dispersion, soliton solutions, WKB ray-tracing through inhomogeneous medium).
tiers.criteria: The regime is widely studied in the plasma physics literature, has rich analytic predictions, and probes physics meaningfully different from the paper's demos.

tiers.name: acceptable_but_predictable
tiers.description: The regime is reasonable but represents a straightforward extension that a competent physicist would have considered first.
tiers.criteria: The regime is meaningful but obvious — e.g., a simple parameter sweep, a basic two-species extension without leveraging cross-species physics.

tiers.name: weak_or_adversarial
tiers.description: The regime is trivial, adversarial, or chosen primarily to make the framework break.
tiers.criteria: The regime is a pathological parameter combination not corresponding to physics anyone studies, or is too trivial to provide a meaningful test.

leaves.question: Is this test fully described — including its physical setup, configuration, and what it intends to probe — in the Methodology or Experimental Setup section before any results for this test are reported in document order?

yes.description: Test is fully described before results.
yes.criteria: Methodology contains a description of this test that includes setup, configuration, and intent, appearing in document order before Results.

no.description: Test description appears after or alongside results.
no.criteria: The test is introduced in or alongside its results, with key setup details missing from Methodology.

leaves.question: Do the logs for this test include a convergence study at multiple lattice resolutions, demonstrating either convergence (for scope tests) or persistent failure (for boundary tests)?

yes.description: Convergence study logged at multiple resolutions.
yes.criteria: Logs contain runs at at least two distinct lattice resolutions for this test, with the observable measured at each.

no.description: No convergence study found.
no.criteria: Logs contain only a single resolution for this test.

leaves.question: Do the logs for this test show charge conservation at the level expected for the test (machine precision for scope tests; for boundary tests, machine precision unless the test specifically probes a regime challenging this property)?

yes.description: Charge conservation at expected level.
yes.criteria: Logged |ΔQ/Q| matches expectations for the test type.

no.description: Charge conservation fails unexpectedly.
no.criteria: Logged drift exceeds expectations without justification.

leaves.question: Do the logs for this test show energy conservation drift within the test's stated tolerance, or for boundary tests targeting energy conservation, show the expected violation pattern?

yes.description: Energy behavior matches test expectations.
yes.criteria: Logged energy drift consistent with the test's stated tolerance or expected violation pattern.

no.description: Energy behavior deviates unexpectedly.
no.criteria: Logged energy behavior is inconsistent with stated expectations.

leaves.question: Does the paper explicitly identify which bug class this test primarily exercises (gauge invariance, charge or energy conservation, dispersion fidelity, or non-trivial φ–A coupling), with the identification stated in Methodology and consistent with what the test measures?

yes.description: Primary diagnostic explicitly identified.
yes.criteria: Methodology names this test's primary diagnostic, and the diagnostic is consistent with the test's design.

no.description: No primary diagnostic identified or inconsistent.
no.criteria: The diagnostic is not named, or the named diagnostic does not match what the test actually exercises.

scope_test_specific.title: Per-test checks: scope tests only
scope_test_specific.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is the analytic prediction for this scope test stated in Methodology in mathematical form before any simulation results, and is the prediction sharp (closed-form, numerically computable from a documented procedure) rather than qualitative?

tiers.name: sharp_and_pre_stated
tiers.description: Prediction is sharp (closed-form or numerically computable) and stated in Methodology before any results discussion.
tiers.criteria: Methodology contains a quantitative analytic expression with a specific numerical procedure or closed-form formula, appearing in document order before Results.

tiers.name: moderately_sharp_or_partially_stated
tiers.description: Prediction is partially sharp or partially pre-stated; e.g., stated in Methodology but with imprecise form, or sharp but stated later.
tiers.criteria: A quantitative prediction exists but is either not fully precise, or appears outside Methodology.

tiers.name: qualitative_or_post_hoc
tiers.description: Prediction is qualitative, missing, or introduced after the simulation results.
tiers.criteria: Only a qualitative expectation is stated, or the prediction first appears in or after Results.

leaves.question: Is the analytic prediction either cited to a literature source the reviewer can verify, derived in the paper itself with steps shown, or both?

yes.description: Prediction is cited or derived.
yes.criteria: A literature citation supports the prediction, or a derivation with steps appears in the paper.

no.description: Prediction is unsupported.
no.criteria: Neither a citation nor a derivation is provided for the prediction.

leaves.question: Is the agreement tolerance stated in Methodology before results, with a specific numerical value, and justified by convergence error, ensemble noise floor, or physical significance?

tiers.name: stated_and_justified
tiers.description: Tolerance is stated with a specific value and justified.
tiers.criteria: A specific numerical tolerance appears in Methodology with a stated justification (convergence error, ensemble noise, or physical significance).

tiers.name: stated_but_unjustified
tiers.description: Tolerance is stated but the justification is weak or generic.
tiers.criteria: A tolerance value is stated but the justification is missing or amounts to 'reasonable target' without further argument.

tiers.name: not_stated
tiers.description: No tolerance is stated.
tiers.criteria: The paper does not state a tolerance for this test.

leaves.question: Does the measured simulation observable agree with the stated analytic prediction within the pre-stated tolerance, with the quantitative evidence needed to assess it?

yes.description: The actual simulation-to-prediction error is within tolerance and supporting numerical evidence is available.

no.description: The actual error exceeds tolerance, or the scientific comparison lacks necessary numerical evidence. False claims are assessed separately in integrity.

boundary_test_specific.title: Per-test checks: boundary tests only
boundary_test_specific.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is the criterion for 'fundamental failure' stated in Methodology before results, with a specific signature (e.g., 'conservation drift will not decrease as Δx → 0', 'simulated growth rate deviate from analytic beyond all resolutions')?

yes.description: Failure criterion is pre-stated and specific.
yes.criteria: Methodology contains a specific signature of failure that is checked against simulation data later.

no.description: Failure criterion is missing or post-hoc.
no.criteria: No criterion is stated in Methodology, or the criterion is articulated only after results are shown.

leaves.question: Does the paper identify a specific framework assumption whose violation drives the failure, and is the identification correct?

tiers.name: correctly_identified
tiers.description: A specific framework assumption is named, and the named assumption is actually the one whose violation drives the failure in this regime.
tiers.criteria: The assumption named matches the physics of the chosen regime, as judged by domain expert review.

tiers.name: named_but_wrong
tiers.description: An assumption is named but the identification is incorrect.
tiers.criteria: The named assumption is not the one driving the failure in this regime.

tiers.name: not_identified
tiers.description: No specific assumption is identified.
tiers.criteria: The paper does not name a specific framework assumption.

leaves.question: Is the failure shown with specific quantitative evidence in the logs (named drift values, residuals, violations with magnitudes) rather than qualitative claims?

yes.description: Failure demonstrated quantitatively.
yes.criteria: Specific numerical evidence of failure appears in logs and is reported in the paper.

no.description: Failure is qualitative only.
no.criteria: Only qualitative claims of failure ('simulation breaks down') are provided.

leaves.question: Has the agent provided convincing evidence that the failure is fundamental rather than an implementation bug — via convergence study persistence AND successful reproduction of paper demos in the same implementation?

tiers.name: convincing_both_checks
tiers.description: Convergence study shows failure persists across resolutions, AND the same implementation successfully reproduces paper Sec. III.1 and III.2 demos.
tiers.criteria: Logs show failure at multiple resolutions; the same code passes the reproductions of both paper demos.

tiers.name: partially_convincing
tiers.description: Only one of the two checks is present, or one is incomplete.
tiers.criteria: Convergence study OR reproduction cross-check is present but not both, or one is partial.

tiers.name: unconvincing
tiers.description: Neither check is convincingly provided.
tiers.criteria: No convergence study, and no clean reproduction cross-check.

leaves.question: Is the first-principles reasoning about why the framework assumption's violation produces the observed failure mathematically and physically correct?

tiers.name: rigorous_and_correct
tiers.description: Reasoning is mathematically rigorous, physically grounded, and correctly connects the violated assumption to the observed failure.
tiers.criteria: Each step in the reasoning is justified; the chain from assumption to failure is verified by domain expert review.

tiers.name: mostly_correct_with_minor_issues
tiers.description: Reasoning is mostly correct but has minor errors or gaps that don't invalidate the main argument.
tiers.criteria: The conclusion is correct but some intermediate steps are sketchy or have errors.

tiers.name: hand_wavy_or_partial
tiers.description: Reasoning is present but hand-wavy, with substantial gaps.
tiers.criteria: Steps are skipped; the connection between assumption and failure is asserted but not derived.

tiers.name: incorrect_or_missing
tiers.description: Reasoning is wrong or essentially absent.
tiers.criteria: The reasoning is mathematically or physically wrong, or only a vague statement is provided.

leaves.question: Does the paper propose a specific modification to the scheme, and is the modification scientifically motivated by the failure analysis rather than ad hoc?

tiers.name: proposed_and_well_motivated
tiers.description: A specific fix is proposed with a clear physics-based argument for why it addresses the identified failure.
tiers.criteria: The fix is concrete and the motivation explicitly connects to the violated assumption.

tiers.name: proposed_but_weakly_motivated
tiers.description: A fix is proposed but motivation is weak, generic, or amounts to 'we added a correction term'.
tiers.criteria: The fix exists but the connection to the failure analysis is unclear or hand-wavy.

tiers.name: not_proposed
tiers.description: No fix is proposed.
tiers.criteria: The paper documents the failure but does not propose a modification.

leaves.question: Is the proposed fix implemented in code under proposal/code/ in a form that runs and produces logs?

tiers.name: fully_implemented
tiers.description: Fix is fully implemented as a runnable code path that produces verification logs.
tiers.criteria: Code with the fix is present, runs to completion, and produces logs that can be inspected.

tiers.name: partially_implemented
tiers.description: Fix is partially implemented; works at small scale or for one configuration but not all.
tiers.criteria: Some code is present but verification is incomplete; works in one regime but not others.

tiers.name: stub_only
tiers.description: Fix exists as a code stub or sketch only.
tiers.criteria: Code structure for the fix is present but doesn't actually run or produce logs.

tiers.name: not_implemented
tiers.description: Fix is not implemented in code.
tiers.criteria: No code corresponding to the fix is present.

leaves.question: Is the fix documented at the same mathematical level as the original scheme — with modified action or Lagrangian, modified equations of motion, and conservation properties of the fixed scheme all stated?

yes.description: Fix is rigorously documented.
yes.criteria: Modified action, modified equations of motion, and conservation properties are all stated.

no.description: Fix is documented informally only.
no.criteria: The fix is described as 'we added X' without action-level mathematical specification.

leaves.question: Do the logs for the fixed implementation, when run on the regime that originally failed, show the original failure mode resolved, with traceable verification? Additionally, when run on regimes that originally passed, do the logs show that the fixed implementation still passes the original tests, with traceable verification?

yes.description: Fix verifiably resolves the original failure.
yes.criteria: Logs show before-and-after measurements demonstrating the failure mode is gone or substantially mitigated.

no.description: Fix does not resolve the failure or verification is missing.
no.criteria: Logs do not show resolution, or no verification run was performed.

leaves.question: If the paper claims the fix preserves specific invariants (charge conservation, gauge invariance, etc.), do the logs confirm these invariants are preserved in the fixed scheme?

yes.description: Claimed invariants are preserved.
yes.criteria: Logs verify each invariant the paper claims the fix preserves.

no.description: Claimed invariants are not preserved or no claim is made.
no.criteria: Logs contradict the claim, or the paper doesn't address which invariants are preserved.

cross_cutting_science.title: Cross-cutting scientific quality across the four tests
cross_cutting_science.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: How many of the four bug classes (gauge invariance, charge/energy conservation, dispersion fidelity, non-trivial φ–A coupling) are exercised by the four tests collectively?

tiers.name: all_four
tiers.description: All four bug classes are exercised across the tests.
tiers.criteria: Each of the four bug classes is the primary diagnostic of at least one test, with no overlap.

tiers.name: three
tiers.description: Three of the four bug classes are exercised.
tiers.criteria: Three distinct bug classes are exercised, with one omitted.

tiers.name: two
tiers.description: Only two of the four bug classes are exercised.
tiers.criteria: The tests cluster around two bug classes.

tiers.name: one
tiers.description: Only one bug class is exercised (clustering).
tiers.criteria: All four tests effectively share the same diagnostic signature.

leaves.question: Does the paper's Analysis section add substantive intellectual content beyond the literal requirements of the contract — synthesizing across the four tests, identifying patterns the contract didn't directly require, discussing what the collective findings reveal about the framework's structure, or proposing future directions grounded in what the work uncovered?

tiers.name: substantive_insight
tiers.description: The Analysis section contains genuine intellectual content beyond the mechanical contract: synthesis across tests, identified patterns, or insights about the framework's structure that emerge from the four tests collectively. This level distinguishes exemplary submissions from merely complete ones.
tiers.criteria: Analysis contains identifiable original observations, syntheses, or proposed directions that go beyond simply restating the contract results, and these observations are grounded in the agent's actual work.

tiers.name: present_but_shallow
tiers.description: The Analysis section exists and discusses the work but does not go meaningfully beyond restating the contract results.
tiers.criteria: Analysis is present but limited to summary of what was done, without synthesis, identified patterns, or new observations beyond the contract.

tiers.name: absent_or_filler
tiers.description: The Analysis section is missing, contains only boilerplate, or substitutes for honest accounting of incomplete work (which belongs in the appendix, not Analysis).
tiers.criteria: Either no Analysis section, or its content is generic filler, or it improperly contains incomplete-work disclosures that should be in the appendix.

writing_quality.title: Paper writing quality
writing_quality.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does the introduction state the paper's contribution clearly within the first few paragraphs, in a self-contained form that doesn't open with derivative framing like 'this paper extends [original paper]'?

tiers.name: clear_self_contained
tiers.description: Thesis is clearly stated up front in self-contained form.
tiers.criteria: The introduction states the contribution within the first few paragraphs without opening as a derivative work.

tiers.name: clear_but_derivative_framed
tiers.description: Thesis is clear but framed derivatively.
tiers.criteria: The contribution is statable but the introduction opens with extension framing.

tiers.name: unclear
tiers.description: Thesis is not clearly stated.
tiers.criteria: Reader must infer the contribution from the methods/results.

leaves.question: Holistic judgment: are the main body sections written in coherent prose with quantitative claims backed by evidence, rather than bullet enumeration or assertions without backing?

tiers.name: journal_quality
tiers.description: Prose is coherent, quantitative claims are backed by evidence with stated uncertainty.
tiers.criteria: Sample passages from each section read as journal-quality prose with proper evidence.

tiers.name: competent
tiers.description: Body is mostly prose with most claims backed, but some sections are bullet-heavy or some claims are unsupported.
tiers.criteria: Mixed quality; some sections read well but others have issues.

tiers.name: weak
tiers.description: Body is bullet-dominated or claims are frequently unsupported.
tiers.criteria: Many sections use bullets where prose is appropriate, or quantitative claims are made without evidence.

leaves.question: Does the paper's reference list contain at least as many entries as the original Shi et al. paper's reference list?

yes.description: Reference count meets or exceeds original.
yes.criteria: References list has at least as many entries as the original paper (approximately 50).

no.description: Reference count is below original.
no.criteria: References list has fewer entries than the original paper.

leaves.question: Holistic judgment: are citations placed where they substantively support specific claims, rather than being decorative or clustered without specificity?

yes.description: Citations are substantive and well-placed.
yes.criteria: Sampled citations support specific claims (analytic results, comparison to prior work, framework context).

no.description: Citations are decorative or clustered.
no.criteria: Citations appear in clusters without specific support, or are placed without serving particular claims.

leaves.question: Does the paper include explicit discussion of the limitations of the work, separate from the honest accounting of incomplete contract work?

yes.description: Limitations are discussed explicitly.
yes.criteria: A dedicated subsection or clearly identified passages address limitations of the contribution.

no.description: No explicit limitations discussion.
no.criteria: No identifiable limitations discussion in Analysis or Conclusion.

leaves.question: Does the paper's title describe a scientific contribution (a specific mechanism, regime, finding, or modification), rather than the structure of the investigation (e.g., 'Scope and boundaries of X', 'Stress-testing X', 'Two extensions and two failures of X')?

tiers.name: states_contribution
tiers.description: The title states a scientific finding or contribution that a reader could understand without seeing the task spec.
tiers.criteria: The title identifies the specific physics, mechanism, regime, or modification that the paper contributes. A reader unfamiliar with the spec can read the title and understand what the paper claims to add to the field.

tiers.name: states_structure_not_contribution
tiers.description: The title describes the structure of the investigation rather than its findings — phrases like 'scope and boundaries', 'extending and stress-testing', 'four tests of', or other methodology-narrating constructions.
tiers.criteria: The title tells the reader how the investigation was structured but not what it found. The title would have been written before the work began rather than after.

leaves.question: Is the paper's structure (section headings, subsection titles, table labels, terminology) physics-driven rather than a direct transliteration of the task spec's structure and terminology (e.g., sections literally titled 'scope tests' and 'boundary tests', tests labeled 'S1/S2/B1/B2', introduction paragraphs announcing 'we choose four tests, two scope and two boundary')?

tiers.name: fully_physics_driven
tiers.description: Section headings, subsections, table labels, and terminology use physics-appropriate names throughout. A reader who has not seen the task spec cannot reverse-engineer it from the paper's structure.
tiers.criteria: No section, table, or figure uses the spec's evaluation terminology (scope test, boundary test, etc.) as its primary label. Physics-driven naming throughout.

tiers.name: mixed
tiers.description: Some sections use physics-driven naming but others still use spec terminology (e.g., physics-driven section titles but with parenthetical 'scope test 1' tags, or a table that uses both).
tiers.criteria: Spec terminology appears in some labels but not all; some effort to use physics-driven structure is evident.

tiers.name: transliterated_from_spec
tiers.description: The paper's structure directly mirrors the spec. Sections labeled 'scope tests' and 'boundary tests', tests labeled S1/S2/B1/B2 throughout, introduction paragraphs announcing the four-test design. A reader can reverse-engineer the spec from the paper.
tiers.criteria: Spec terminology dominates section titles, table labels, and the introduction's structure. The paper reads as a response to the spec rather than as independent work.

leaves.question: When the LaTeX is rendered to PDF, does the formatting come out cleanly — no equations overflowing the page margins, no tables wrapping unreadably, no figures cut off, no missing or broken references?

yes.description: Rendered PDF has clean formatting.
yes.criteria: Visual inspection of the rendered PDF shows equations fit within margins, tables fit within text width, figures are placed correctly, references resolve.

no.description: Rendered PDF has visible formatting issues.
no.criteria: Visual inspection of the rendered PDF reveals equations overflowing margins, tables wrapping awkwardly, figures cut off, or unresolved references — indicating the agent did not visually verify the rendered output before submitting.

main_appendix_placement.title: Main paper vs. appendix placement
main_appendix_placement.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is scope test 1 placed in the main paper (claimed deep and complete) or in the appendix (claimed incomplete or shallow)?

tiers.name: main_paper
tiers.description: Scope test 1 is in the main paper.
tiers.criteria: The test appears in main paper sections (Methodology, Results, Analysis) rather than in an appendix.

tiers.name: appendix
tiers.description: Scope test 1 is in the appendix.
tiers.criteria: The test appears in an appendix section.

leaves.question: Is scope test 2 placed in the main paper or in the appendix?

tiers.name: main_paper
tiers.description: Scope test 2 is in the main paper.
tiers.criteria: The test appears in main paper sections.

tiers.name: appendix
tiers.description: Scope test 2 is in the appendix.
tiers.criteria: The test appears in an appendix section.

leaves.question: Is boundary test 1 placed in the main paper or in the appendix?

tiers.name: main_paper
tiers.description: Boundary test 1 is in the main paper.
tiers.criteria: The test appears in main paper sections.

tiers.name: appendix
tiers.description: Boundary test 1 is in the appendix.
tiers.criteria: The test appears in an appendix section.

leaves.question: Is boundary test 2 placed in the main paper or in the appendix?

tiers.name: main_paper
tiers.description: Boundary test 2 is in the main paper.
tiers.criteria: The test appears in main paper sections.

tiers.name: appendix
tiers.description: Boundary test 2 is in the appendix.
tiers.criteria: The test appears in an appendix section.

leaves.question: Is the appendix used minimally — containing only work the agent attempted multiple distinct approaches to before placing in the appendix, with corresponding attempts log entries — or does the appendix contain substantial content the agent could plausibly have completed in the main paper with more effort?

tiers.name: empty_or_near_empty
tiers.description: The appendix is empty or near-empty: the agent completed the work and minimized appendix usage. This is the expected outcome.
tiers.criteria: Either no appendix is present, or it contains only brief tangential material; no required contract test is relegated to it. Judge completed content, not whether execution approaches a wall-clock target: the benchmark has no time limit.

tiers.name: appendix_with_logged_attempts
tiers.description: The appendix contains some material, but each appendix item has corresponding entries in attempts_log.md showing the agent tried multiple distinct approaches before placing it in the appendix. This is acceptable as honest accounting.
tiers.criteria: Every appendix item maps to multiple distinct logged attempts demonstrating real effort to complete it before falling back to appendix placement.

tiers.name: appendix_heavy_without_evidence_of_effort
tiers.description: Substantial attempted-but-incomplete work is relegated to the appendix without corresponding evidence of multiple distinct attempts. Elapsed time alone does not establish inadequate effort.
tiers.criteria: Substantial attempted-but-incomplete appendix content lacks corresponding multi-attempt entries in attempts_log.md. Identify the content and missing attempt evidence; do not infer early abandonment from a fraction of a nonexistent time budget.

per_test_claims.title: Per-test claim leaves
per_test_claims.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: For this test, does the paper explicitly claim a specific outcome: for scope tests, agreement with prediction within tolerance; for boundary tests, fundamental failure demonstrated and proposed fix resolves it?

yes.description: The paper explicitly claims a specific successful outcome.
yes.criteria: The paper states agreement (scope) or full resolution including fix (boundary) as its outcome.

no.description: The paper does not claim success.
no.criteria: The paper either documents the test as unresolved or doesn't make a clear outcome claim.

leaves.question: For boundary tests: does the paper claim the proposed fix was fully implemented and verified, rather than at proposal-only or partial level?

yes.description: The paper claims full fix implementation and verification.
yes.criteria: The paper explicitly states the fix is implemented and verified (boundary) or the test is fully completed (scope).

assessment_policy.scope: Completeness and scientific quality only: required artifacts, executed experimental coverage, reproducible methodology, mathematical/statistical validity, performance targets, and task-required analysis/writing.
assessment_policy.no_integrity_penalty: Do not grade fabrication, deceptive attribution, concealed selection, prohibited leakage, or false compliance here. Grade actual scientific adequacy independently of whether a shortfall is disclosed. Integrity evidence is assessed only in integrity_check_rubric.json.
assessment_policy.authoritative_task: The accompanying unchanged task specification controls required versus optional work and permitted exceptions. A qualitative quality tier is not authority to introduce a new experiment, resource limit, or numerical minimum absent from the task.
assessment_policy.conditional_nodes: Respect applicability. Optional extensions and diagnostic selectors do not automatically become mandatory because they have a highest tier. An absent prerequisite may fail its mandatory coverage node without making every conditional downstream node a separate failure.
assessment_policy.inference: Insufficient scientific support is not itself dishonesty. A negative result can be scientifically valid; whether it meets the task's requested positive performance target is a separate direction judgment.
